summary.headline: TMB posted record Q2 FY27 net profit of INR451 crore (+42.09% YoY) on 27.25% business growth, with net NPA at 0.14%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 as its eighth straight quarter of beating the prior quarter's growth, with total business up 27.25% YoY to INR1,30,237 crore and net profit at a record INR451 crore. Net interest income rose to INR807 crore and NIM was 4.19%, down about 10 bps QoQ as term-deposit mix and refinance (about INR1,000 crore at 7-7.5%) pushed up funding costs. The bank made full provisions for SMA-1 and SMA-2 ahead of ECL norms effective 1 April 2027, with provisions of INR304.24 crore against an estimated INR385 crore ECL requirement. Management raised FY27 floors for deposits (20%+) and advances (22%+), and guided NIM at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR29,280 crore, of which agri about INR22,000 crore and retail about INR6,084 crore. Portfolio LTV 62.35%; about 3.1% of book would be above market value on a 20% gold price fall; gold loan SMA-0-to-3 at risk about INR28 crore (0.10%).

segments.name: Advances and MSME
segments.commentary: Advances up 29.32% to INR60,691 crore; MSME growth 23.62%. Unsecured exposure about 20 bps; the uptick was a loan to Kerala State Electricity Board secured against cash flows. About 52% of advances are repo-linked, 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 25.49% to INR69,546 crore, with term deposits up about 29%. Non-callable deposits were 40.62% of incremental term deposits (INR7,570 crore in H1). FCNR(B) raised about USD51.94 million; 1-year FCNR(B) rate now about 4.25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth floor raised to 20%+ from earlier 18%+; advances growth floor 22%+; CASA growth about 17% in H2.
NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, versus the earlier 4% guidance.
Cost to income expected to rise from 38.28% but stay well below 44% as branches open and IT investment continues.
Target of 60 branch openings in FY27 (9 opened in H1), with 20+ outside Tamil Nadu by year-end.
Long-term aim is to grow 4-5 percentage points faster than the industry over the next 3-5 years.
CD ratio can rise to 98% against 87.27% currently, given net worth of 12.53% of the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Nine branches opened in H1 FY27; 60 planned for the year, with 37 opened YoY (15 outside Tamil Nadu).
Business per employee at INR25 crore; profit per employee about INR35 lakh.
Ongoing IT investment and data/process automation cited as drivers of productivity and cost pressure.
Leverage ratio 11.99% vs 3.50% requirement; LCR 139.43%; NSFR 146.15%.
demand_pricing: Investment portfolio rose to about 22% of the balance sheet, yielding about 7% vs about 10.3% on advances, which weighed on margin mix.
Repo cut passthrough is automatic at each loan's quarterly reset; the 25 bps repo move flows to the 5.5% benchmark over about three months.
Refinance of about INR1,000 crore taken from SIDBI at 7-7.5% during the quarter.
Bulk deposits are 19% of total deposits; the bulk share of the INR7,570 crore incremental term deposits was not disclosed on the call.
Management sees no material oil-price impact so far on export credit or MSME books; drought risk is being monitored through daily gold LTV tracking.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of gold loans between agri and retail, and how much of the book is repo-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans total INR29,280 crore: agri about INR22,000 crore and retail INR6,084 crore. About 52% of advances are repo-linked (reset quarterly), 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank sustain high growth and how is the oil price affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: The target is to grow 4-5 percentage points above industry growth over 3-5 years, not a fixed 20-30% rate. No oil-price impact seen yet in export credit or MSME.

qa_highlights.question: How has NIM and yield on advances moved, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield on advances rose to 10.32% from 10.10% as advances were repriced to offset higher deposit costs. NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, with management calling it a floor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost to income ratio rise, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to income is expected to move up from 38.28% due to branch openings and IT spend, but to stay well below 44%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI insurance norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission is only about INR9 crore in H1. Management estimated about a 20% reduction in that income, which incremental business would offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the disputed share ownership matter, and would it block a bonus or split?
qa_highlights.answer: The Appellate Tribunal order dated 9 July has not been appealed by the bank or ED within the window. The bank has applied to RBI to regularise the share transfer, and management said this does not block a bonus or split.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure from term-deposit mix shift and refinance; NIM guided lower to 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps.
ECL norms from 1 April 2027: estimated INR385 crore requirement vs INR304.24 crore provisions held (about 80% cover).
Gold price volatility: gold traded above USD4,000 an ounce; the bank cut per-gram valuation by about INR800 in recent days.
Pending RBI decision on regularising the disputed share transfer (FEMA issue).
Cost-to-income drift upward from branch expansion and IT spend, plus IRDAI commission impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profit and asset quality, with a repeated message that guidance numbers are floors. Noticeably defensive on NIM mix, the FCNR(B) deposit size and the bulk-deposit breakdown, which management said it would follow up on later.
key_quotes: And this growth has driven a strong net profit, the highest ever, INR451 crores highest ever net profit.
What we are looking for is to exceed the industry growth by a certain percentage.
And I would say 4.10% plus/minus 5 basis is what we are looking for the rest of the year.
We have provided a provision available of INR304.24 crores against the INR385 crores that is required to cover the expected credit loss.

adds.what: 60 branch openings planned in FY27 (9 opened in H1), 20+ outside Tamil Nadu by year-end

growth.why: Management raised FY27 advances growth floor to 22%+ and deposit growth to 20%+, backed by 9 branches opened in H1 of a 60-branch FY27 plan and 27% business growth in Q2, though no specific capacity or order numbers were given beyond branch openings.
